question: What species, site, and study details are disclosed in the official CvSU newsletter announcement of Patrique Erika Cancel’s 2024 microplastics conference paper?

source.title: Cancel presents paper at 11th International Conference on Fisheries and Aquaculture 2024
source.provider: Cavite State University, Office of the Vice President for Research and Extension; REconnections, Vol. 7 No. 9 (September 2024)
source.reviewedContent: CvSU newsletter article text and its study summary.
source.studyTitleAsPrinted: Detection and Characterization of Microplastics in Mullet Fish (Mugil cephalus) in Maragondon Estuary
source.conferenceAsReported: 11th International Conference on Fisheries and Aquaculture 2024, 26-27 September 2024.
findingsAsSummarized: The newsletter reports microplastics in fish scales, gills, and guts and names fragments, fibers, pellets, filaments, and films.
It reports a correlation between microplastics in fish organs and those in sediment and water, and says polypropylene was the dominant polymer.
These are claims summarized in an institutional newsletter; the underlying paper and data were not obtained or independently checked.

boundedQueries: site:cvsu.edu.ph "Detection and Characterization of Microplastics" "Maragondon Estuary"
"Detection and Characterization of Microplastics in Mullet Fish"
retrieval.outcome: The official CvSU newsletter announcement was located. The bounded public search did not locate the underlying conference paper/abstract, a sample-level dataset, or a methods/station appendix. This search limit does not establish that those materials do not exist.
retrieval.distinction: The separate ASEANO end-project proceedings mention unidentified CvSU fish-tissue microplastics research in Bacoor, without study title or taxa. No source links that Bacoor remark to this Maragondon Estuary paper; treat them as separate leads.

evidenceLimits: No sample count, collection date, station name or coordinates, sampling protocol, fish identification method, voucher, or per-fish results table is supplied by the reviewed newsletter summary.

The species/site information is not promoted to an occurrence assertion; historical research context does not establish current presence, abundance, catchability, natural diet, legal status, water safety, or inventory completeness.
No estuary boundary or salinity classification can be inferred from the newsletter.
No item-specific reuse terms for the newsletter article or underlying study were verified.
nextAction: Seek the full conference paper/abstract or an authorized CvSU research record with study dates, sample size, station-to-waterbody crosswalk, identification support, methods, and reuse terms. Continue separately seeking the identity and deliverable for the Bacoor fish-tissue study and the completed Ternate Marine Park BMS/BAMS records. Do not send an inquiry without separate authorization.
